research.investment_thesis: VTI is the most mandate-compliant instrument available: ~3,600 holdings, a 0.03% expense ratio, deep liquidity and no single-name risk. Price has held the 50-day average on a retest and momentum has turned back up, while the position would be the account's first and only exposure.
research.bull_case: Broad, cheap, liquid exposure with no issuer risk; the support retest held and the trend structure is intact; entry at a modest discount to the recent high.
research.bear_case: The macro backdrop is unverified this cycle, cap-weighting concentrates roughly a third of assets in ten mega-cap names, and a broad-market entry inherits that correlation.
primary_risks: mega-cap concentration inside a nominally diversified fund
single-position account: no diversification across holdings yet
research.what_could_make_this_wrong: A rate-path surprise or an earnings-led repricing of the mega-cap complex.
research.why_doing_nothing_may_be_better: Cash carries no drawdown risk and the account has no clock forcing it to be invested.
missing_information: FRED macro series unavailable (no API key)
no fundamentals pass for an ETF instrument
research.entry_logic: Single tranche of roughly one third of the account at the current quote, regular hours only.
research.exit_logic: Reviewed if the position falls 12% from cost or the drawdown ladder reaches WARNING.
research.expected_holding_period: indefinite; this is a core-style long-term holding
